label: input j in the first three positions of the original sequence
explanation: Fires only when the input token is the letter j during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase, and only near the start of the sequence: about 3.2% of steps at t=0, 1 and 2 (the rate among j inputs there is high), a few weak firings at t=3, and none at t>=4. Magnitude falls off steeply with position: j at t=0 always gives the max (~1.74), t=1 gives about 1.0, and t=2 is weak (~0.2-0.5). That is why t=0 holds 54% of the mass, t=1 33%, t=2 13% and t=3 under 1%. It never fires on the delimiter or in the copy phase, including when j is fed back as a copy-phase input, and it never fires on any other token. Previous tokens, length L and digit count have no clear effect beyond what position explains.

issues: Minor: t=3 firings are real but weak. On test, about 2.3k active steps (0.6% of activation mass) are missed, all at t=3 on input j, with activations of about 0.05-0.17 of max. Adding j at t=3 hurts badly: precision 0.14 for that slice, and t<=3 with first occurrence gives F1 0.874. Leaving t=3 out is the right call, and the explanation already notes it.

Minor: about 5% of predicted j at t=2 are inactive (848 false positives on test, e.g. 'g 2 j', 'n n j'). These look like scattered weak-tail failures with no consistent preceding token, and they don't depend on j having appeared earlier: for j at t=2 that is not its first occurrence, precision is 0.72 on only 1032 steps.

Verified: zero activation in the delimiter and copy phases, including j fed back as a copy-phase input (j with phase!=0 has precision 0 over 90,875 steps). It fires only on in_tok j. Activation mass by position is t0 54%, t1 33%, t2 13%, t3 0.6%, and zero for t>=4. Adding the first-occurrence condition lowers test F1 to 0.959, which matches the claim that the plain predicate is best.
Test scores reproduce: precision 0.983, recall 0.955, F1 0.969, mass recall 0.994.
